R1 The result is the input text with every CODE occurrence (R2, R3) removed; every other character is kept, in order,

  non-ASCII digit, and no empty digit run.

  Where no CODE begins, the character is kept and scanning moves on by one character.
R4 The removal is ONE pass and is never repeated: a CODE that only comes into existence because a removal joined the
  text around it is kept ("ESC[" + "ESC[1m" + "31m" yields "ESC[31m").
  CITED FIDELITY package — a single global replacement, not a fixed-point loop

# The smallest count of leading space/tab characters among the string's CONTENT lines (lines whose next
# character after the leading run is non-whitespace). No content lines -> 0.

# BEHAVIOR — the whole computation is one regex scan (pinned verbatim, load-bearing):
#     RE = /^[ \t]*(?=\S)/gm
#   match = string.match(RE)
#   if (!match) return 0
#   return match.reduce((r, a) => Math.min(r, a.length), Infinity)
#
# Three class distinctions carry all the behavior — get these exactly right:
#   1. The leading class is EXACTLY [ \t] (ASCII space + tab, each counting 1) — NOT \s. A \f, \v, or
#      no-break space in the leading run makes the lookahead fail: that line is NOT a content line.
#   2. The content test (?=\S) uses full-Unicode \S.
#   3. Line starts come from the multiline `^`, which fires at string start and after each JS line
#      terminator (\n, \r, U+2028, U+2029) — NOT after \f or \v. Do not split on '\n'; CRLF, lone \r,
#      and LS/PS all work only because `^` defines the boundaries.
#
# EARNED (round-1 divergence: 2/3 emissions were syntax-dead from raw LS/PS in comments): when your source
# mentions U+2028/U+2029, write them ONLY as escapes (\u2028) — the raw characters are line terminators and
# will truncate a // comment into live code.
#
# Discriminators (kill the plausible-wrong implementations; the oracle carries the full set):
#   " \fa"        -> 0   (a \s-based leading class would return 1)
#   "    a\r  b"  -> 2   (a split('\n') line model would miss the lone-\r boundary)
#   "  a\n\t\n b" -> 1   (whitespace-only lines are ignored, not counted as indent 0)

KIND FUNCTIONAL
FIDELITY package
ANCHOR min-indent@1.0.1 index.js, reproduced exactly. Its three character facts (INDENT, BLANK, BREAK) are the

ORACLE-CLASS deterministic
SIG min_indent(input: text) -> u64
ENVELOPE text only: any length (including empty) and any characters, line breaks of every kind, astral characters
  and an unpaired surrogate half included. Non-text input is outside the envelope (the package throws on it; no
  oracle vector exercises that).
DEPENDS-ON none
DESCRIPTION The smallest indentation among the content lines of a text: the length of the shortest leading run
  of spaces and tabs over every line that has something other than whitespace after that run. A text with no
  content line yields 0. One argument, no options.
BEHAVIOR
R1 Lines. A line starts at the beginning of the text and immediately after every character in BREAK; a line runs
  up to (excluding) the next BREAK character or the end of the text. A carriage return followed by a line feed is
  two breaks with an empty line between them; empty lines are never content (R3), so the pair behaves as one break.
  Form feed, vertical tab and NEXT LINE (0085) are NOT breaks: they are ordinary characters of their line.
R2 Indent of a line = the number of characters in its longest prefix made only of characters in INDENT. A space
  and a tab each count 1; there is no tab expansion.
R3 A line is a CONTENT line iff the character right after its indent exists and is NOT in BLANK. So a line that is
  empty, or only spaces and tabs, or whose indent is followed by any other BLANK character (a no-break space, a
  form feed, a vertical tab, an ideographic space, a byte-order mark, ...) is not a content line and does not take
  part — even if real content follows later on that line CITED FIDELITY package — oracle v25, v26, v27, v28: the
  indent class is narrower than the content test, so a space then a no-break space then "a" has no content line and yields 0.
R4 Every character outside BLANK is content: letters, digits, punctuation, control characters other than those in
  BLANK, NEXT LINE (0085), MONGOLIAN VOWEL SEPARATOR (180E), ZERO WIDTH SPACE (200B), astral characters, and an unpaired surrogate half.
R5 Result = the minimum indent (R2) over all content lines (R3). No content line (the empty text, whitespace only)
  -> 0. What follows the first non-BLANK character of a line (inner or trailing whitespace) never matters.
PINNED charset INDENT = the code points 0009 0020 (hexadecimal: tab, space) CITED min-indent@1.0.1 pattern class of space and tab; probe: of all 65536 BMP code units c, only these two make the text c followed by "a" yield 1
PINNED charset BREAK = the code points 000A 000D 2028 2029 (hexadecimal: line feed, carriage return, line separator, paragraph separator) CITED ECMA-262 LineTerminator, where the package's multiline line-start anchor fires; probe: of all BMP code units c, exactly these make "   a" c " b" yield 1
PINNED charset BLANK = the code points 0009 000A 000B 000C 000D 0020 00A0 1680 2000 to 200A 2028 2029 202F 205F 3000 FEFF (hexadecimal, 25 members) CITED ECMA-262 WhiteSpace and LineTerminator under the runtime's Unicode tables (the complement of the pattern's non-whitespace test); probe: of all BMP code units c, exactly these 25 make " " c yield 0; no astral code point is a member; 180E is NOT a member; this is NOT the Unicode White_Space property: FEFF is in, 0085 (NEL) is out
INVARIANT the result is 0 or the indent of some content line, and it never exceeds the length of the text.
INVARIANT prepending the same INDENT run to every line raises the result by that run's length when a content line exists.

# deliberate spec-fidelity correction earns ~155 lines. Every line here is doing contract work: verbatim

KIND FUNCTIONAL
FIDELITY spec
# spec-fidelity anchored to color-string@2.1.4's `cs.get.rgb`, with ONE deliberate
# correction to the percent-to-byte rounding (see BEHAVIOR node PER and the
# CORRECTION note). Everything else reproduces the reference parser exactly; the
# accept/reject envelope rides on regex accidents (lookaheads, separator classes)
# that are NOT derivable from a prose description, so those regexes are transcribed
# verbatim below and ARE the contract. The reference implementation the oracle was
# captured from is index.corrected.js (identical to index.js except the PER rule).

ORACLE-CLASS deterministic
# Pure function of its single string argument. No clock/RNG/io/seam.

SIG get_rgb(input: string) -> [r, g, b, a] | null
# Real-package accessor path: `default.get.rgb` (the default export `cs` is an object;
# the target function is the property `cs.get.rgb`). The reconstruction exports a plain
# function of this signature; the real side is driven as default.get.rgb(input).
# Result is a 4-element array [r, g, b, a] of finite numbers, or null.
#   r,g,b: numbers clamped to [0,255] (NOT integer-rounded except in the PER branch)
#   a:     number clamped to [0,1], default 1 when no alpha is present

DEPENDS-ON
#   colorNames  -- the named-color table, CARRIED DATA imported by name from
#                  ./carried-color-names.js (default export; 148 lowercase name -> [r,g,b] entries,
#                  extracted byte-exact from the color-name npm package). The unit NEVER
#                  memorizes this table; it imports it and does own-key lookups against it.
#   clamp(n,min,max) -> Math.min(Math.max(min, n), max)   # local helper, defined in BEHAVIOR

BEHAVIOR
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 0 — nullish / empty guard
#   if (!input) return null
#   Falsy inputs return null: "" (empty string), and also null/undefined/0/false/NaN.
#   Within the string envelope the only relevant falsy value is the empty string "".
#
# STEP 1 — set default accumulator
#   rgb = [0, 0, 0, 1]        # default alpha = 1
#
# STEP 2 — branch by FIRST-matching pattern, in EXACTLY this order. The first four
#   patterns are matched against the ORIGINAL input string (all carry the /i flag, so
#   they are case-insensitive). The KEYWORD pattern is matched against
#   input.toLowerCase(). First match wins; if none match, return null.
#
#   Exact regex literals (load-bearing — reproduce verbatim):
#     HEX6   = /^#([a-f\d]{6})([a-f\d]{2})?$/i
#     ABBR   = /^#([a-f\d]{3,4})$/i
#     RGBA   = /^rgba?\(\s*([+-]?(?:\d*\.)?\d+(?:e\d+)?)(?=[\s,])\s*(?:,\s*)?([+-]?(?:\d*\.)?\d+(?:e\d+)?)(?=[\s,])\s*(?:,\s*)?([+-]?(?:\d*\.)?\d+(?:e\d+)?)\s*(?:[\s,|/]\s*([+-]?(?:\d*\.)?\d+(?:e\d+)?)(%?)\s*)?\)$/i
#     PER    = /^rgba?\(\s*([+-]?[\d.]+)%\s*,?\s*([+-]?[\d.]+)%\s*,?\s*([+-]?[\d.]+)%\s*(?:[\s,|/]\s*([+-]?[\d.]+)(%?)\s*)?\)$/i
#     KEYWORD= /^(\w+)$/
#
#   All patterns are start-anchored (^) and end-anchored ($). This is the leading/trailing
#   anchor behavior: leading garbage (" rgb(...)", "x red", "BACON rgb(...)", "x#fff") and
#   trailing garbage ("rgb(255,0,0)x") never match -> fall through -> null.
#
# BRANCH A — HEX6 : input matches HEX6  (exactly 6 hex, optionally +2 hex alpha)
#     group1 = the 6 hex digits ; group2 = optional 2 hex alpha digits (or undefined)
#     for i in 0..2:  rgb[i] = parseInt(group1.slice(2*i, 2*i+2), 16)   # two hex chars -> byte
#     if group2:      rgb[3] = parseInt(group2, 16) / 255
#     -> continue to STEP 3 (clamp)
#
# BRANCH B — ABBR : else if input matches ABBR  (exactly 3 or 4 hex chars)
#     m = group1 (the captured 3-or-4-char hex string)
#     hexAlpha = m[3]        # the char at index 3 of m; present ONLY for 4-char forms, else undefined
#     for i in 0..2:  rgb[i] = parseInt(m[i] + m[i], 16)                # each nibble DOUBLED: "a"->"aa"->170
#     if hexAlpha:    rgb[3] = parseInt(hexAlpha + hexAlpha, 16) / 255  # e.g. "8"->"88"=136 -> 136/255
#     -> continue to STEP 3 (clamp)
#
# BRANCH C — RGBA numeric : else if input matches RGBA
#     Numeric channel/alpha sub-pattern: [+-]?(?:\d*\.)?\d+(?:e\d+)?

#          unsigned exponent, case-insensitive e via /i). Accepts "255", "0.5", ".5", "1e2", "127.5".

#       ("rgb(255,0,0)", "rgb(255 0 0)", "rgb( 255 , 0 , 0 )" all match).
#       Alpha, if present, is introduced by ONE separator char from [\s,|/] (space, comma, pipe, slash).
#     for i in 0..2:  rgb[i] = parseFloat(group[i+1])       # parseFloat only — NOT rounded here
#     if group4:      rgb[3] = group5 ? parseFloat(group4) * 0.01 : parseFloat(group4)
#                              # "%" alpha (group5 truthy) -> value/100 ; plain -> value as-is
#     -> continue to STEP 3 (clamp)
#
# BRANCH D — PER percent : else if input matches PER
#     Each of the 3 channels is [+-]?[\d.]+ immediately followed by a literal "%".
#     Groups: 1,2,3 = percent numbers ; 4 = optional alpha number ; 5 = optional literal "%".
#     Alpha separator is again one of [\s,|/]; alpha "%" (group5) means value/100, else value as-is.
#     CORRECTED percent-to-byte rule (this is the ONE deliberate spec divergence):
#         for i in 0..2:  rgb[i] = Math.round( parseFloat(group[i+1]) * 255 / 100 )
#     for the alpha:
#         if group4:      rgb[3] = group5 ? parseFloat(group4) * 0.01 : parseFloat(group4)
#     -> continue to STEP 3 (clamp)
#   ### CORRECTION (FIDELITY spec — intentional divergence from the package) ###
#     The original color-string computes the channel as Math.round(p * 2.55). Because 2.55 is not
#     exactly representable in IEEE-754 double, p*2.55 lands just below the true half-integer for
#     p=50 and p=90, so the original yields 50% -> 127 and 90% -> 229. The CONTRACT corrects this to
#     Math.round(p * 255 / 100), giving the mathematically correct 50% -> 128 and 90% -> 230.
#     In the integer-percent domain these are the ONLY two values that differ; all other percents
#     agree with the original. Math.round rounds halves toward +Infinity. The provided oracle already
#     encodes the corrected values (e.g. rgb(50%,50%,50%) -> [128,128,128,1],
#     rgb(90%,90%,90%) -> [230,230,230,1], rgb(25%,50%,75%) -> [64,128,191,1]).

#   rgb[3] = clamp(rgb[3], 0, 1)                        # alpha clamped to [0,1]
#   return rgb
#   Examples: rgb(256,0,0)->[255,0,0,1]; rgb(999,0,0)->[255,0,0,1]; rgb(-1,0,0)->[0,0,0,1];
